function.name: list_directory
function.description: List files and folders in a directory on the user's local PC. Defaults to current working directory '.'.

path.description: Relative or absolute directory path to list (default is '.').

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the contents of a file on the user's local PC. Supports plaintext, code, CSV, Excel (.xlsx/.xlsm), PDF (.pdf), Word (.docx), and PowerPoint (.pptx).

path.description: Relative or absolute path to the file to read.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with content.

path.description: Relative or absolute path to the file to create/overwrite.

content.description: The exact plaintext or code content to write into the file.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Search and replace a specific block of text/code within an existing file.

path.description: Relative or absolute path to the file to edit.

old_text.description: The exact string block currently in the file that you want to replace.

new_text.description: The replacement string block to insert.

function.name: run_powershell
function.description: Run a PowerShell command on the user's local PC in the current working directory (e.g. git, pytest, builds, dir). Returns exit code, stdout and stderr. The user must manually approve every command, so keep each one purposeful.

command.description: The PowerShell command line to execute.

function.name: read_clipboard
function.description: Read the text currently copied to the user's Windows clipboard. Ideal when the user copies an email, paragraph, table, or snippet and asks you to summarize, fix, or act on it.

function.name: write_clipboard
function.description: Copy text directly onto the user's Windows clipboard so they can immediately Ctrl+V paste it into Outlook, Word, or Teams.

text.description: The text to place onto the Windows clipboard.

function.name: open_file
function.description: Launch/open a document or folder in its default Windows application (e.g., Word, Excel, PDF reader, File Explorer) after creating or updating it so the user can review it immediately.

path.description: Relative or absolute path to the document or folder to open.

function.name: write_docx
function.description: Create or overwrite a Microsoft Word (.docx) document from Markdown-formatted text. Supports #/##/### headings, bullet lists (- ), numbered lists (1. ), **bold** text, and Markdown tables (| col | col |).

title.description: Optional document title heading at the top of the page.

content.description: Markdown-formatted body content to render into the Word document.

function.name: fill_docx_template
function.description: Fill placeholders (such as '{{DATE}}', '{{SUBJECT}}', '[NAME]') inside an existing Word (.docx) template (preserving headers, footers, tables, and formatting) and save to a new .docx file.

template_path.description: Path to the existing .docx template file.

output_path.description: Path where the filled .docx file should be saved.

replacements.description: Key-value dictionary mapping exact placeholder strings to their replacement text.

function.name: update_excel
function.description: Create a new Excel (.xlsx) workbook or update an existing one by appending rows to a sheet and/or setting specific cell coordinates (e.g. {'B4': 'Complete', 'C4': 100}).

path.description: Path to the .xlsx file (created automatically if it does not exist).

sheet_name.description: Optional target worksheet name (defaults to active sheet, or creates sheet if missing).

append_rows.description: Optional list of rows (each row is a list of cell values) to append to the bottom of the sheet.

cell_updates.description: Optional dictionary mapping cell coordinates (like 'A1', 'C5') to new values.

function.name: write_pptx
function.description: Create or overwrite a PowerPoint (.pptx) presentation from a list of slides. Each slide can have a title, subtitle, bullets, speaker notes, a table, and an image. Pass template_path to build on an existing deck or template so the result uses its theme and layouts. To change an existing deck, use edit_pptx instead.

path.description: Relative or absolute path for the .pptx file to create or overwrite.

layout.description: Slide layout name from the deck or template, e.g. 'Title Slide', 'Title and Content', 'Title Only'. Omit to choose automatically.

bullets.description: Body text, one entry per paragraph. Indent an entry with two leading spaces per level for sub-bullets.

table.description: Table rows; the first row is the header.

image_path.description: Path to a .png or .jpg file to place on the slide.

template_path.description: Optional .pptx or .potx file whose theme, master and layouts the new deck should use.

keep_template_slides.description: Keep the slides already in the template and add the new ones after them (default false: start empty).

function.name: edit_pptx
function.description: Change an existing PowerPoint (.pptx) presentation: replace text, set a shape's or table cell's text, set speaker notes, and add, delete or reorder slides. Read the file first: read_file shows each slide's layout and every shape's [id].

path.description: Path to the existing .pptx file to change.

operations.description: Edits applied in order; slide numbers refer to the deck as it stands at that step. Each is an object with 'op' and its fields: replace_text {find, replace, slide?} replaces text everywhere (or on one slide), keeping formatting; set_text {slide, shape, text, row?, col?} sets a shape's text by the [id] shown in the outline (row and col for a table cell; one paragraph per line, two leading spaces per indent level); set_notes {slide, text}; add_slide {at?, layout?, title?, subtitle?, bullets?, notes?, table?, image_path?}; delete_slide {slide}; move_slide {slide, to}.

function.name: search_files
function.description: Search recursively across a directory tree by filename pattern and/or inside file contents (searches plaintext, code, CSV, Word .docx, Excel .xlsx, PDF .pdf, and PowerPoint .pptx in one call).

path.description: Root directory to search from (default is current directory '.').

query.description: Optional case-insensitive text or keyword to search for inside files and filenames.

file_pattern.description: Optional filename filter or glob pattern (e.g. '*.docx', '*.xlsx', '*memo*', default '*').

max_results.description: Maximum number of matching files to return (default 30).

function.name: list_inbox
function.description: List recent emails in the user's Classic Outlook Inbox (returns Subject, ReceivedTime, Unread status, Categories, and EntryID). Supports filtering by unread status or subject keywords.

max_items.description: Maximum number of emails to return (default 25, max 100).

unread_only.description: If true, only return unread emails (default false).

subject_filter.description: Optional case-insensitive substring to filter email subjects.

function.name: get_calendar
function.description: Read the user's Classic Outlook Calendar appointments and meetings for today and upcoming/past days (returns Subject, Start, End, Location, AllDayEvent, and BusyStatus).

days_ahead.description: Number of days ahead from today to include (default 7).

days_back.description: Number of days in the past to include (default 0).

function.name: open_email
function.description: Pop open a specific Outlook email (or a Reply window for it) on the user's screen using its EntryID from `list_inbox`.

entry_id.description: The exact EntryID string of the email from `list_inbox`.

open_reply_window.description: If true, opens a Reply draft window for the email instead of just viewing it (default false).

function.name: create_draft_email
function.description: Create a new draft email in Classic Outlook and pop it open on the user's screen ready for review and manual sending. Never auto-sends.

subject.description: Subject line for the draft email.

body.description: Plaintext body of the draft email.

to_hint.description: Optional recipient email address or name.
